title: UiPath's Agentic Pivot Is Paying Off
subtitle: Shares rebounded roughly 39% from their May lows as ARR nears $2 billion and the company reframes itself as the orchestration layer for AI agents, not the vendor of brittle screen-scraping robots.
summary: UiPath closed fiscal 2026 with its first full year of GAAP profitability, beat on the top and bottom line in Q1 FY2027, and raised full-year guidance to roughly $1.78 billion. With ARR near $1.9 billion, a fortress balance sheet, and a fresh $500 million buyback, the stock has rebounded ~39% from its May lows as the agentic automation narrative takes hold.

bodyHtml:
UiPath spent the better part of two years being written off as the poster child for a category that generative AI supposedly made obsolete. The tape has flipped. Shares have rebounded roughly 39% from their May lows, and the stock is trading near its highs as investors reward the company's successful reframing — from vendor of brittle screen-scraping robots to orchestration layer for the agentic era.

The numbers support the narrative shift. UiPath closed fiscal 2026 with its first full year of GAAP profitability, a milestone the business had chased since going public, and one that separates it from most AI-adjacent software names still burning cash. Annual recurring revenue stands near $1.9 billion and is closing in on the $2 billion mark, while trailing twelve-month revenue checks in around $1.67 billion. The company is no longer a turnaround story; it is a compounding software business with a clean income statement.

Q1 FY2027, reported in late May, reinforced the momentum. Revenue of $418 million beat expectations, and earnings of $0.15 per share came in ahead of the $0.13 consensus estimate — the kind of beat that used to be routine for UiPath and had gone missing during the rough patch. Management responded by raising full-year guidance to roughly $1.78 billion, signaling confidence that the acceleration is durable rather than a one-quarter artifact.

The balance sheet is the quiet part of the bull case. UiPath holds about $1.3 billion in cash against just $83 million in debt, leaving roughly $1.22 billion in net cash and an enterprise value near $5.4 billion against a market cap around $6.6 billion. Trailing free cash flow of roughly $375 million gives the company ample dry powder for acquisitions or organic investment. A fresh $500 million buyback authorized in March — following completion of a prior $1 billion program — shows management is putting that cash to work rather than hoarding it.

On valuation, the stock still looks reasonable for a business growing at this pace. The trailing P/E sits near 21, but the forward multiple compresses to roughly 14 as analysts build in the raised guidance. Against a market cap around $6.6 billion and trailing revenue near $1.67 billion, the revenue multiple is a fraction of what pure-play AI names command. The Street remains cautious overall — consensus is a Hold with a mean target near $13.25 — though Needham upgraded to Buy in March with a $15 target, and the gap between price and targets has narrowed as the stock rallied.

The product strategy is what separates this recovery from prior false dawns. UiPath for Coding Agents launched to let enterprises run Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents inside its orchestration and governance layer, positioning the platform as the connective tissue for agentic development rather than a competitor to the model labs. The Agentic ERP offering built with Deloitte extends Maestro and Agent Builder into record-to-report, source-to-pay, and lead-to-cash workflows, giving finance chiefs a governed path from assisted automation to autonomous operations.

A Snowflake Cortex AI integration promises autonomous data-to-action pipelines that close the loop between analytics and execution. Each move pushes UiPath further up the stack, from automating clicks to orchestrating decisions.

Risks remain, and the Hold consensus reflects them. Big platform vendors are embedding agentic capabilities into products UiPath's customers already own, and the coding-agent market is evolving fast enough that today's partnerships could look dated within a year. Microsoft and Salesforce loom largest, and both have distribution advantages UiPath cannot match. But the company's position as the model-agnostic governance and orchestration layer is arguably stronger than its old RPA moat ever was, and the market is beginning to price that in.

For investors, UiPath offers a rare combination in the AI trade: a profitable, cash-generative franchise with a fortress balance sheet and a forward earnings multiple in the mid-teens. That is a stark contrast to the narrative-driven valuations of pure-play AI infrastructure names. If agentic automation adoption accelerates along the product roadmap, the rebound from the May lows could be the first chapter rather than the last. The fundamentals have done the talking; now it is up to the market to listen.

Disclosure: The Signal holds no position in PATH. Positions may change. This is not financial advice.
